[[File:Louis Bertrand (1731-1812).png|thumb|Louis Bertrand]]
'''Louis Bertrand''' ({{IPA|fr|lwi bɛʁtʁɑ̃}}; 3 October 1731 – 15 May 1812) was a Genevan [[mathematician]].

== Biography ==
Bertrand was born on 3 October 1731 in [[Geneva]], [[Republic of Geneva]], the son of Antoine Bertrand, a merchant and banker, and Madeleine Lafont.<ref name="HDS">{{HDS|025850|Louis Bertrand|author=Fernando Vidal|date=24 September 2002}}</ref> He studied in Geneva and under [[Leonhard Euler]] in [[Berlin]].<ref name="HDS"/> Bertrand was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Geneva]] from 1761 to 1795, and was its [[Rector (academia)|rector]] in 1783.<ref name="HDS"/> He became a member of Geneva's [[Council of Two Hundred]] in 1784, and served in the National Assembly in 1795 during the Genevan revolutionary period.<ref name="HDS"/>

In 1778, Bertrand published the work ''Developpement nouveau de la partie elementaire des mathematiques'', which included a demonstration of [[Euclid's postulates]] that gained fame before the rise of [[non-Euclidean geometry]] and influenced most of the [[elementary geometry]] treatises of the 19th century.<ref name="HDS"/> In 1774, he published the ''De l'instruction publique'' in open opposition to [[Horace Bénédict de Saussure]]'s ''Projet de réforme pour le [[Collège de Genève]]''.<ref name="HDS"/> He worked, besides in Geneva, also in Berlin, [[Bern]], and [[London]].<ref>{{cite web |date=6 September 2022 |publisher=[[Consortium of European Research Libraries]] |title=Bertrand, Louis |url=https://data.cerl.org/thesaurus/cnp00581695}}<!-- auto-translated from unknown (Italian or Spanish) by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Bertrand died  on 15 May 1812 in Geneva, aged 80.<ref name="HDS"/>
